newsitem.title: JAPAN: Canon profits hit record high on PC boom, weak yen.
newsitem.headline: Canon profits hit record high on PC boom, weak yen.

text.p: Canon Inc., a leading manufacturer of cameras, printers and photocopiers, said Wednesday it earned record profits in 1996, drawing strength from the global boom in personal computers and the weaker yen.
Canon said 1996 group net profits rose a dramatic 71 percent to 94.2 billion yen ($759 million), well above the previous record of 61.4 billion yen ($495 million) in 1990.
Group sales also set a record in 1996 for the third year in a row, rising 18 percent to 2.56 trillion yen ($20.6 billion).

The company expected the good news to continue this year, forecasting that healthy sales of computer printers would help propel net profits to 100 billion yen ($806 million) in 1997, with sales hitting 2.78 trillion yen ($22.4 billion).
"Computer peripherals such as bubble-jet printers and laser printers will remain brisk, helping push up sales," a Canon director told reporters.
The company said last year's introduction of new bubble-jet models boosted sales of printers for home use, while office-use laser printers also registered brisk sales.

Buoyed by a worldwide personal computer boom, revenues in Canon's office equipment division rose 17.4 percent in 1996 to 2.1 trillion yen ($16.9 billion), or more than 80 percent of total group sales.
The weaker yen also helped buoy Canon's earnings last year by increasing revenues from exports.
"The weaker yen rate raised our pre-tax profit estimate for this year by 16 billion yen ($129 million)," he said.

Canon President Fujio Mitarai said in an interview last Friday that his company should be able to expand its group sales to four trillion yen ($32.2 billion) in calendar 2000 if the yen does not surge back to around 110 yen to the dollar. It is now at 124 to the dollar.
He also said Canon aims to become the global market leader among printer manufacturers.
At present, Hewlett-Packard Co. holds about half of the world's ink-jet printer market, followed by Canon's 30 percent, analysts said.
